mainTopic: The loaf case in the תוספתא, and the חכמים' 24-hour rule for a woman who finds blood: its reason, its measure, and how it fits רבי דוסא's view
overview: The amud opens by finishing the loaf case from the תוספתא. The loaf is טהור because we assume a person moved it, and we do not make the same assumption about a raven, since a raven does not act on purpose. The גמרא then defends the ruling against the rule that a ספק טומאה ברשות היחיד is טמא. It gives two answers: a loaf is a דבר שאין בו דעת לישאל, or the טומאה there is only דרבנן, which the word מדף supports. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה. A ברייתא explains that the חכמים rejected both שמאי and הלל. Their rule is that a woman who finds blood is impure backward for the shorter of 24 hours or the time since her last check. After רבה's reason ('she would feel it') is set aside, the real reason turns out to be a rabbinic enactment: women check every morning and evening, so a woman who skipped her checks loses an extra עונה. רב פפא challenges this, and the גמרא explains the fixed 24 hours in two ways: a uniform measure, or so that the sinner should not gain. Finally, the גמרא asks whether the משנה about a woman with a וסת follows only רבי דוסא, and it narrows the dispute with the רבנן in two different ways.

steps.title: A pure person moved the loaf
steps.stepSummary: The loaf found on the floor is טהור because we assume a טהור person came in and moved it down.
steps.simpleTranslation: For I say: a pure person went in there and took it down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why the loaf in the תוספתא is טהור. It is not because we never assume טומאה moves around. It is because a person probably took the loaf down from the shelf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaf was on a shelf above an impure מדף. If it had simply fallen, it would have hit the impure item. Since a person could have lifted it and set it on the floor, the loaf never touched the טומאה, so it stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For I say': we assume this likely explanation of what happened
A ritually pure person
A loaf of bread

phrases.english: For I say:
a pure person entered there and took it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the loaf. He took it off the shelf and put it on the floor, so it never fell onto the impure item.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אָדָם טָהוֹר נִכְנַס לְשָׁם וּנְטָלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation, started before this section, of why the loaf case is טהור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reasoning: a likely human action explains the case, rather than a general rule against assuming טומאה moved.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loaf is טהור because a person likely moved it safely.

steps.title: Why not say a raven threw it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, in the basket case, we don't say a raven brought the שרץ in, just as we say a person moved the loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, let us say a raven came and threw it in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If we can imagine a person moving the loaf, why not imagine a raven dropping the שרץ into the basket in the basket case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the basket case we do assume the טומאה was there all along. The challenge is that this seems inconsistent. If we accept an outside explanation for the loaf, we should accept one for the basket too: a raven dropped the שרץ in after the produce was already emptied out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here too, let us say': we should apply the same logic here
A raven, a bird that often handles dead creatures
Threw or dropped

phrases.english: Here too, let us say:
phrases.notes: 'Here' points back to the earlier case of the basket where the dead שרץ was found.

phrases.english: a raven came and threw it in!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי נֵימָא: עוֹרֵב אֲתָא וּשְׁדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 1 by applying it to the basket case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between the loaf case and the basket case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an outside explanation (a person) can save the loaf, an outside explanation (a raven) should save the basket.

steps.title: People act on purpose, ravens don't
steps.stepSummary: We assume a deliberate act from a person, but not from a raven, which does not act with purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a person, who acts with intent, we say it. About a raven, which does not act with intent, we don't say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A person acts on purpose, so we can say he picked the loaf up. A raven does not act on purpose, so we do not credit it with such an action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the loaf down carefully is a purposeful act that fits a human being. Imagining a bird that happened to drop a שרץ into the basket at exactly the right moment is too random to rely on. So the two cases are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: With intent, on purpose
Without intent, not on purpose
We say, we assume

phrases.english: A person, who acts with intent, we say it;
a raven, which acts without intent, we do not say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָדָם דִּבְכַוָּנָה — אָמְרִינַן, עוֹרֵב דְּשֶׁלֹּא בְּכַוָּנָה — לָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the raven challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases: purposeful human action versus random animal action.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any outside explanation, human or animal, should be equally acceptable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a purposeful human action is assumed. A raven's random action is not.
steps.whatToRemember: We may assume a person did something on purpose to explain a case. We do not assume the same about an animal like a raven.

steps.title: Isn't a doubt in a private domain impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the loaf ruling: this is a ספק טומאה ברשות היחיד, which should make it טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, this loaf is a case of doubtful impurity in a private domain, and any doubtful impurity in a private domain is ruled impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against the ruling itself. The loaf's status is a doubt, the doubt happened ברשות היחיד, and the known rule says such a doubt is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that a ספק טומאה ברשות היחיד is treated as טמא. The loaf might have fallen onto the impure מדף, or a person might have moved it. That is exactly such a doubt in a private place. So the loaf should be טמא, not טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now, after all': opens an argument from known facts
A doubt whether something became impure
A private domain
Its doubt is ruled impure

phrases.english: Now, this loaf
is a doubtful impurity in a private domain,
and any doubtful impurity in a private domain —
its doubt is impure.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves the question unspoken: so why did the תוספתא call the loaf טהור?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי הַאי כִּכָּר סְפֵק טוּמְאָה בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the raven discussion and challenges the basic ruling of the loaf case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תוספתא's ruling that the loaf is טהור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule says a ספק טומאה ברשות היחיד is טמא. The loaf case fits that rule, so it should be טמא.

steps.title: An object that can't be asked stays pure
steps.stepSummary: The loaf is a דבר שאין בו דעת לישאל, and such a doubt is טהור even in a private domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is an object without the awareness to be asked, and any object without the awareness to be asked, whether in a public or a private domain, its doubt is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the private-domain rule does not apply here. A loaf has no mind and cannot be asked what happened, and for such objects the doubt is טהור everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a doubt ברשות היחיד is טמא applies only when the subject has דעת, meaning it could be asked about what happened, like a person. A loaf has no awareness. For things like that, the doubt is טהור whether it happened in a private or a public domain.

keyTerms.meaning: An object with no awareness, which cannot be asked what happened
A public domain
Its doubt is ruled pure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the private-domain rule makes every doubt טמא. It only applies to someone or something with דעת that could be asked. An object without awareness, like a loaf, follows the opposite rule: its doubt is טהור.

phrases.english: Because it is an object
that has no awareness to be asked,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל,
phrases.english: and any object that has no awareness to be asked,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד —
phrases.english: whether in a public domain or in a private domain —
its doubt is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule: the private-domain rule does not cover objects without awareness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every ספק טומאה ברשות היחיד is טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: A דבר שאין בו דעת לישאל is טהור in any domain, so the loaf is טהור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic principle of ספק טומאה: whether the doubtful subject has awareness changes the ruling.

steps.title: Second answer: only rabbinic impurity
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, the loaf case involves only a טומאה דרבנן, where a doubt is treated leniently.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: here we are dealing with impurity that is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the private-domain challenge. The impure item under the loaf was only טמא מדרבנן, so we can be lenient about the doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict rule for a ספק טומאה ברשות היחיד applies to טומאה דאורייתא. When the טומאה is only rabbinic, a doubt is ruled טהור. This answer works even without the 'cannot be asked' principle from step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say': introduces an alternative answer
Impurity that comes from rabbinic law, not Torah law

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
here it is about rabbinic impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָכָא בְּטוּמְאָה דְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 4, alongside the answer in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the טומאה involved is only rabbinic.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the טומאה is דרבנן, the doubt is ruled טהור even ברשות היחיד.

steps.title: The word מדף shows a light impurity
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא's word מדף is like 'עלה נדף', a light, driven leaf, which hints at a light, rabbinic טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, since it teaches 'מדף', as it is written: 'עלה נדף', a driven leaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the second answer from the wording of the תוספתא. It calls the impure item a מדף, a word related to 'נדף', something light like a leaf blown by the wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מדף comes from the same root as נדף in the פסוק 'עלה נדף'. That points to a 'light' kind of טומאה, meaning טומאה דרבנן. So the text itself fits the claim that this case involves only rabbinic impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is also precise': the wording supports this answer
A light impurity, here understood as rabbinic
A driven, wind-blown leaf: something light

steps.whatToRemember: The loaf is טהור for two possible reasons: a loaf has no awareness to be asked, or the טומאה was only דרבנן. The word מדף supports the second reason.

phrases.english: It is also precise, since it teaches 'madaf',
phrases.notes: 'It' means the תוספתא's wording, which called the impure item under the shelf a מדף.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'a driven leaf'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second answer from step 6 using the wording of the תוספתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the loaf case involves טומאה דרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תוספתא's term מדף, read in light of 'עלה נדף' in ויקרא 26:36

steps.title: Why the חכמים rejected both שמאי and הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה and brings a ברייתא explaining why they did not follow שמאי or הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The חכמים say: not like this one and not like that one.' A ברייתא explains: not like שמאי, because he made no safeguard for his rule. And not like הלל, because he went beyond the proper limits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה: the view of the חכמים. It quotes a ברייתא that gives the reason the חכמים rejected both earlier opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי said the woman is impure only from when she sees blood. That gives no protection in case the bleeding really began earlier. הלל made her impure all the way back to her last check, even if that was many days ago. That protects too much and causes too much loss. So the חכמים are looking for a middle path.

keyTerms.term: לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה
keyTerms.meaning: Not like this opinion and not like that opinion
A fence or safeguard, a protective rule
He went beyond the proper limits; he overdid it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים disagree that a safeguard is needed. They agree with הלל that one is needed. They only think הלל's safeguard is too big.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: Not like the words of this one, etc.
The Sages taught:
And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה,
phrases.english: Not like the words of this one and not like the words of that one,
not like the words of Shammai —
for he did not make a safeguard for his words,
and not like the words of Hillel —
for he went beyond his bounds.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about doubtful טומאה and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים reject שמאי for having no safeguard, and they reject הלל for having an excessive one.

steps.title: The חכמים' middle rule: the shorter time wins
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים rule that the 24-hour period and the time since the last check each cut the other short, so whichever is shorter applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the 24-hour period shortens the time from check to check, and the time from check to check shortens the 24-hour period.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the חכמים' own rule. A woman who finds blood is impure backward, but only for whichever is shorter: 24 hours or the time since her last check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible limits. One is a full day back (מעת לעת). The other is back to her last clean check (מפקידה לפקידה). Each one limits the other, so she never goes back further than either one allows.

keyTerms.meaning: From time to time; a full 24-hour period
A self-examination (a check for blood)
From one examination back to the previous examination
Cuts down, shortens

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים' rule: go back whichever is shorter, 24 hours or the time since the last check.

phrases.english: Rather, a twenty-four-hour period reduces
the time from examination to examination,
phrases.notes: 'עַל יָד' literally means 'by hand.' Here, together with מְמַעֶטֶת, it just means 'shortens.'

phrases.english: and from examination to examination reduces
the twenty-four-hour period.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מֵעֵת לְעֵת מְמַעֶטֶת עַל יָד מִפְּקִידָה לִפְקִידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting both views, the ברייתא gives the חכמים' own middle-ground rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She is impure backward for the shorter of 24 hours or the time since her last examination.

steps.title: Example: when 24 hours is the shorter limit
steps.stepSummary: If her last clean check was days ago, she is impure only for the last 24 hours, not all the way back to that check.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does the 24-hour period shorten the time since the last check? She checked herself on Sunday and was clean. She did not check on Monday or Tuesday. On Wednesday she checked and found blood. We do not say she is impure back to Sunday's check, only for the last 24 hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives an example of the first half of the rule. Here the last check was long ago, so the 24-hour limit is the shorter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under הלל's view, she would be impure back to Sunday, which is several days. The חכמים cut that down to just 24 hours. This is where they disagree with הלל's 'going too far.'

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces an example)
The first day of the week, Sunday
She becomes impure (backward in time)

phrases.english: A twenty-four-hour period reduces
the time from examination to examination — how so?
She examined herself on Sunday
and found that she was pure,
and she sat through Monday and Tuesday and did not examine herself,
and on Wednesday she examined herself and found that she was impure —
we do not say she is impure from examination to examination,
but rather for a twenty-four-hour period.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעֵת לְעֵת מְמַעֶטֶת עַל יָד מִפְּקִידָה לִפְקִידָה, כֵּיצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the first half of the rule from step 9 with a concrete case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the last check was more than 24 hours earlier, she is impure only for the 24 hours before.

steps.title: Example: when the last check is the shorter limit
steps.stepSummary: If she had a clean check just a few hours ago, she is impure only back to that check, not for a full 24 hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does the time since the last check shorten the 24 hours? She checked herself in the first hour and was clean. She did not check in the second and third hours. In the fourth hour she checked and found blood. We do not say she is impure for 24 hours, only back to her last check.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives an example of the second half of the rule. Here the last clean check was only a few hours earlier, so that check is the shorter limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clean check proves she was pure at that moment. So there is no reason to go back a full day. She is impure only for the three hours since the clean check.

keyTerms.meaning: The first hour of the day
Pure / impure

steps.whatToRemember: A clean check always sets a floor: she can never be impure from before a check that showed she was pure.

phrases.english: And from examination to examination reduces
the twenty-four-hour period — how so?
She examined herself in the first hour
and found that she was pure,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָשְׁבָה לָהּ שְׁנִיָּה וּשְׁלִישִׁית וְלֹא בָּדְקָה,
phrases.english: and she sat through the second and third hours and did not examine herself,
and at the fourth hour she examined herself and found that she was impure —
we do not say she is impure for a twenty-four-hour period,
but rather from examination to examination.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּקִידָה לִפְקִידָה מְמַעֶטֶת עַל יָד מֵעֵת לְעֵת, כֵּיצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the second half of the rule from step 9, the mirror image of step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When she had a clean check within the last 24 hours, she is impure only back to that check.

steps.title: Why teach something so obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: of course a woman who checked clean an hour ago is not impure for a full 24 hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! Since she checked herself an hour ago and was found clean, we do not make her impure for a full 24 hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ruling from Step 11 seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clean check is clear proof she was pure at that moment. So nobody would think to make her impure for a time when we know she was clean. Why would the ברייתא spell this out?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?
A full 24-hour period going backward
We declare impure

phrases.english: It is obvious!
Since she examined herself at the first hour
phrases.notes: This means a check done shortly before she found blood, as in Step 11.

phrases.english: and found that she was pure,
we do not render her impure for twenty-four hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why the ruling of Step 11 needed to be stated
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's second case (recent clean check limits the 24 hours)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A clean check proves purity at that time, so stating it adds nothing

steps.title: It was taught to match the first case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא taught the obvious case only so it would parallel the first case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it taught that the 24-hour period cuts short the time back to the last check, it also taught that the time back to the last check cuts short the 24-hour period.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second case is there for balance with the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real new idea is the first case: a woman who has not checked in days is impure only for 24 hours. Once the ברייתא said that, it also wrote the mirror-image case for completeness, even though that one is obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it already taught (this, it also taught that)
From one check back to the previous check
Shortens, cuts down

phrases.english: Since it taught that a twenty-four-hour period
reduces the time from examination to examination,
it also taught that from examination to examination
reduces the twenty-four-hour period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second case must teach something new
steps.terutzMaskana: It was written only to mirror the first case

steps.title: רבה's suggested reason: a woman can feel a flow
steps.stepSummary: רבה suggests the חכמים limit her impurity because a woman feels when blood comes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What is the reason of the חכמים? A woman feels it within herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: why do the חכמים rule the way they do? רבה gives a first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's idea is that a woman would notice a flow, so we do not need to worry that blood came out long ago without her knowing. This would explain why we do not go all the way back to her last check.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their reason?
The חכמים of the משנה
Feels within herself (that blood is flowing)

phrases.english: Rabba says:
What is the reason of the Rabbis?
A woman senses within herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the reasoning behind the חכמים' rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים rely on the fact that a woman feels a flow

steps.title: אביי: then she should be impure only from now
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that if she feels it, she should be impure only from the moment she saw blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, it should be enough to count from her moment of seeing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's reason by pushing it to its logical end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a woman always feels a flow, then the moment she noticed is the moment it started. That is the view of שמאי, not the חכמים. So רבה's reason cannot explain why the חכמים go back 24 hours at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (then this follows)
Her moment is enough: impure only from when she saw blood

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If so, her time should be sufficient!
phrases.notes: This is exactly שמאי's view from the משנה, which the חכמים did not accept.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's reason in Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reason that a woman feels a flow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reason proves too much: it leads to שמאי's view, with no going back at all

steps.title: רבה was only testing אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבה did not truly mean that reason; he wanted to sharpen אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה only wanted to sharpen אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבה said a reason that does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה was אביי's teacher and uncle. He gave a weak reason on purpose to see if אביי would catch the flaw, and אביי did. So the weak reason was never really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: To sharpen (someone's mind)

phrases.english: And Rabba wanted to hone Abaye.
phrases.notes: He said something on purpose to see whether אביי would spot the problem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts אביי's challenge and explains why רבה said it
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the statement as a teaching test
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה did not really mean it; אביי's objection stands

steps.title: So what is the real reason?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבה's reason fails, the גמרא asks again for the reason of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the question and is setting up the real answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The search has to start over now that the reason about feeling a flow was dropped. The answer must explain why she goes back exactly 24 hours, no more and no less.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, so then (starting over)

phrases.english: Rather, what is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reopens the question after רבה's reason is set aside
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The true reason for the חכמים' 24-hour rule

steps.title: שמואל: women were told to check morning and evening
steps.stepSummary: The answer rests on a rabbinic rule that women check themselves twice a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the חכמים set up for Jewish women to check themselves morning and evening. The morning check protects the pure items from the night, and the evening check protects the pure items from the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its real answer by bringing a rabbinic rule from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each check covers the time-block before it: morning covers the night, evening covers the day. A clean check means the טהרות she touched in that block stay pure. This sets up the next step about a woman who skipped these checks.

keyTerms.meaning: Set up a rule (a rabbinic enactment)
Morning and evening
To make fit, to keep valid
Pure items (food and objects kept in purity)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: As that which Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel says:
The Sages instituted for the daughters of Israel
that they should examine themselves morning and evening,
morning, to render fit the pure items of the night,
and evening, to render fit the pure items of the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The basis is the rabbinic rule to check twice daily

steps.title: She skipped her checks, so she loses an עונה
steps.stepSummary: A woman who did not check as she should is penalized by losing the pure items of an עונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this woman, since she did not check, loses an עונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer: because she did not do the required checks, she loses a time-block of purity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 24-hour rule is a rabbinic consequence of skipping the twice-daily checks. That is why it is not based on when the blood actually started.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
She lost
A time-block: a day or a night

phrases.english: And this one, since she did not examine herself,
phrases.notes: This is the woman in the משנה who did not have regular periods and found blood.

phrases.english: she loses a period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies שמואל's rule to explain the חכמים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Skipping the required checks costs her an עונה of purity

steps.title: What does losing an עונה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what עונה means here, since one עונה is only half of 24 hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does עונה mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the word עונה, setting up its explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One עונה is only a day or a night, about 12 hours. But the חכמים make her impure for a full 24 hours, so the word seems not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: What is (meant by)?

phrases.english: What is a "period"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of Step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How losing one עונה matches a 24-hour impurity

steps.title: An extra עונה: together 24 hours
steps.stepSummary: עונה means an additional עונה, which together with the current one makes 24 hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: An extra עונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that she loses one extra time-block on top of the current one, making a full 24 hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She already loses the current day or night she was in. The penalty for not checking adds one more block before it. Two blocks of about 12 hours equal the 24 hours of מעת לעת.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra, additional

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים' 24-hour rule is a rabbinic penalty: women should check every morning and evening, so a woman who did not check loses one extra עונה. That adds up to 24 hours. It is not based on the idea that she would feel the blood.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think one עונה equals 24 hours. An עונה is a day or a night; the 24 hours are the current עונה plus one extra.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the 24-hour impurity comes from a rabbinic enactment, the twice-daily checks, and not from a worry about when the blood actually began.

phrases.english: An additional period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She loses one extra עונה beyond the current one, totaling 24 hours

steps.title: רב פפא: Twenty-four hours can cover three periods
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, speaking to רבא, challenges the explanation that 'an עונה' means one extra עונה, so that two עונות together make 24 hours. Sometimes a 24-hour stretch actually touches three עונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: But sometimes you find three day-or-night periods inside one 24-hour stretch!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the answer from step 21. That answer said the penalty of 'an extra עונה' adds up to exactly 24 hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עונה is a daytime or a nighttime. If a woman checks in the middle of the day, going back 24 hours reaches into the middle of the day before. That stretch touches three עונות (part of today, last night, and part of yesterday), so 'two עונות' and 'מעת לעת' do not always match.

keyTerms.meaning: A period of time: either a daytime or a nighttime
A full 24-hour stretch, from this time yesterday to this time today
Sometimes

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
But sometimes you find
phrases.notes: For example, if she checks at midday, 24 hours back reaches midday yesterday, which touches three periods.

phrases.english: three periods within a 24-hour stretch!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim from step 21 that two עונות always equal 24 hours
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that 'an עונה' means one extra עונה, making exactly מעת לעת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 24-hour stretch that starts mid-period can touch three עונות, so counting עונות and counting 24 hours give different results

steps.title: The חכמים made one equal measure for all
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים set one standard measure of 24 hours for everyone, so the rule would not change from case to case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים made their measures equal, so that the rule would not be split up; it is always 24 hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא. The חכמים chose one fixed measure, a full מעת לעת, for every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count of עונות can differ depending on when she checks. To avoid a messy rule that changes each time, the חכמים set one uniform measure of 24 hours. Sometimes this touches three עונות, and that is accepted for the sake of one clear rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים made their measures equal, giving one uniform rule
So that you should not divide or make distinctions

phrases.english: The Sages made their measures equal,
so that you should not make distinctions, rather it is a 24-hour stretch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The penalty should be counted in עונות, so it should change with the time of the check
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים set a fixed 24 hours for everyone, even when it touches three עונות

steps.title: Second answer: The sinner should not gain
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the 24-hour rule exists so that a woman who delayed her check does not end up better off than one who checked on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you like, say: the reason is so that the sinner should not profit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to רב פפא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule were 'one extra עונה', a woman who checks early in the morning would lose a full 24 hours. A woman who waited until noon would lose less time. That would reward the one who delayed, so the חכמים fixed 24 hours for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: If you like, say instead (introduces another answer)
So that a sinner should not gain from his wrongdoing

phrases.english: If you like, say:
so that the sinner should not profit.
phrases.notes: The 'sinner' is the woman who did not check twice a day as she should (step 18).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא חוֹטֵא נִשְׂכָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reason, alongside step 23, for the fixed 24 hours
steps.terutzResolutionType: Penalty reason: no reward for delaying
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Counting by עונות would be fair
steps.terutzMaskana: Counting by עונות would help the woman who delayed, so 24 hours is fixed

steps.title: What is the difference between the two answers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the two answers lead to any practical difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step by asking when the two answers would give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers explain the 24-hour rule. The גמרא wants a case where one answer applies and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers of steps 23 and 24
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the uniform-measure reason and the no-gain-for-sinner reason lead to different results

steps.title: The difference: A woman who was prevented from checking
steps.stepSummary: The answers differ when a woman was held back by circumstances beyond her control and so did not check.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is when she was prevented and did not check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 25 with a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the 'no gain for the sinner' reason, a woman who could not check is not a sinner, so she would lose only one extra עונה. Under the 'one equal measure' reason, the 24 hours apply to everyone, so she would still lose a full מעת לעת.

keyTerms.meaning: She was prevented by forces outside her control
She checked herself

steps.whatToRemember: The 24-hour rule has two reasons. A uniform measure means 24 hours for everyone. No gain for the sinner means 24 hours only for a woman who really neglected to check. They differ when she could not check.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where she was prevented and did not check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A woman who was unable to check: under the uniform-measure reason she still loses 24 hours, but under the sinner reason she loses only one extra עונה

steps.title: Does the משנה follow only רבי דוסא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about a woman with a fixed cycle and suggests it follows רבי דוסא alone, against the other view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Any woman who has a fixed cycle, etc.' Shall we say our משנה follows רבי דוסא and not the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. It suggests the line follows one side of a dispute, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a woman with a וסת is impure only from the moment she sees blood, with no backward impurity. The גמרא suggests this matches only רבי דוסא's opinion. If so, the משנה would not follow the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed, regular cycle for a woman's period
Shall we say? (suggests a conclusion that may be pushed back)
Our משנה

phrases.english: 'Any woman who has a fixed cycle,' etc.
Shall we say our Mishnah is Rabbi Dosa,
and not the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי דּוֹסָא הִיא, וְלָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 24-hour topic and turns to the next line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's ruling about a woman with a וסת follows only one side of a dispute

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי אליעזר and רבי דוסא disagree
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the dispute. רבי אליעזר limits 'her time is enough' to four kinds of women. רבי דוסא gives it to any woman with a fixed cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says, four women are impure only from the time they see: a girl who never had a period, a pregnant woman, a nursing woman, and an old woman. רבי דוסא says: any woman with a fixed cycle is impure only from the time she sees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that is the basis for its suggestion in step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה's ruling about a woman with a וסת matches רבי דוסא's words exactly. רבי אליעזר's list of four women does not include a woman with a fixed cycle. So it looks like the משנה follows רבי דוסא and not the other view.

keyTerms.meaning: Their time is enough: they are impure only from the moment they see blood, not before
Here, a girl who has never had a period
A pregnant woman
A nursing mother

steps.confusionAlert: Here בְּתוּלָה does not just mean an unmarried girl. It means a girl who has never yet had a period.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Four women, their time is enough:
a virgin, a pregnant woman, a nursing woman, and an old woman.
Rabbi Dosa says:
Any woman who has a fixed cycle,
her time is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind the suggestion of step 27
steps.raayaObject: The claim that our משנה follows רבי דוסא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי דוסא, unlike רבי אליעזר, says any woman with a וסת is impure only from the time she sees

steps.title: The משנה can follow everyone: the רבנן agree when she sees at her usual time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the רבנן argue with רבי דוסא only when the woman sees blood not at her usual time. Our משנה is about blood at her usual time, so everyone agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows the רבנן. They argue with רבי דוסא only when she sees blood not at the time of her cycle. But when she sees at the time of her cycle, they agree with him. Our משנה is talking about seeing at the time of her cycle, so it is everyone's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the claim from step 27 that the משנה follows only רבי דוסא. It says the משנה can fit the רבנן too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trick is to make the argument smaller. If the רבנן agree to דיה שעתה when she sees at her usual time, then the משנה, which deals with that case, is agreed by all. The argument stays only for blood that comes at an unusual time.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say: the view you thought disagrees may actually fit
They only argue in this one case: a way of making a dispute smaller
At the time of her fixed cycle
They agree with him
Everyone's opinion

phrases.english: You may even say it follows the Rabbis.
The Rabbis disagree only
with Rabbi Dosa
when it is not at the time of her cycle,
but at the time of her cycle they agree with him,
phrases.notes: They agree that 'her time is enough': she becomes impure only from when she saw, not earlier.

phrases.english: and our משנה is about the time of her cycle,
so it is everyone's opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion in step 27, using the ברייתא from step 28, by limiting where the dispute applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the dispute (אוקימתא of the argument)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'her time is enough' for a woman with a fixed cycle fits only רבי דוסא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן agree when she sees at her usual time, and the משנה is about that case, so it fits everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא about stains seems to follow only the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: If the argument is only about blood at an unusual time, then רבי דוסא gives דיה שעתה even then. But a ברייתא says that blood at an unusual time makes her impure for 24 hours back. That ברייתא would then have to follow the רבנן and not רבי דוסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This means רבי דוסא says 'her time is enough' even when it is not at the time of her cycle. If so, who taught this ברייתא: A woman with a fixed cycle — her stain is impure going backward, because if she sees blood not at the time of her cycle, she makes things impure for 24 hours back. Shall we say it follows the רבנן and not רבי דוסא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 29. It shows that the answer forces a ברייתא to go against רבי דוסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 put the argument only in the unusual-time case, so רבי דוסא must say דיה שעתה there too. The ברייתא says plainly that at an unusual time she is impure מעת לעת. So the ברייתא cannot follow רבי דוסא, and the גמרא is uneasy about that.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication: from what was just said, it follows that
Who is the תנא that taught this? Which view does this source follow?
A blood stain found on a garment, not a flow she felt
Going backward in time
A full 24-hour period counted backward
Shall we say? It brings up a conclusion the גמרא would rather avoid

phrases.english: This implies that Rabbi Dosa
says it even when it is not at the time of her cycle?
Then who taught this
that the Rabbis taught in a ברייתא:
A woman who has a fixed cycle
— her stain is impure going backward,
phrases.notes: Going back to when the garment was last washed.

phrases.english: because if she sees blood not at the time of her cycle
she makes things impure for the 24 hours before.
Shall we say it follows the Rabbis
and not Rabbi Dosa?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי דּוֹסָא אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת וִסְתָּהּ אֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from step 29's answer and shows it clashes with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 29, which puts the dispute only in the unusual-time case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי דוסא gives דיה שעתה even at an unusual time, the ברייתא, which says she is impure מעת לעת at an unusual time, must go against him.

steps.title: The ברייתא can follow רבי דוסא, so the משנה follows רבי דוסא alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the narrowing. רבי דוסא argues only when she sees at her usual time. At an unusual time he agrees she is impure for 24 hours back. So the ברייתא fits him, and the משנה, which is about her usual time, follows רבי דוסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the ברייתא follows רבי דוסא. He argues with the רבנן only when she sees at the time of her cycle. But when it is not at the time of her cycle, he agrees with them. Our משנה is about the time of her cycle, and it follows רבי דוסא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 30 by making the argument smaller in the opposite direction. Now the ברייתא fits רבי דוסא, but the משנה belongs to רבי דוסא only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the argument was placed in the unusual-time case. Now it is placed in the usual-time case: רבי דוסא says דיה שעתה there, and the רבנן still say מעת לעת. Everyone agrees about the unusual-time case, so the ברייתא is fine, but the משנה is no longer agreed by all.

keyTerms.meaning: He argues against them
He agrees with them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two answers. Step 29 says the argument is only about the unusual time, so the משנה fits everyone. Step 31 says the argument is only about the usual time, so the משנה fits רבי דוסא alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer brings us back to the idea from step 27, that the משנה follows רבי דוסא. Now, though, it comes with a clear limit: even רבי דוסא agrees to מעת לעת when the blood comes at an unusual time.

phrases.english: You may even say it follows Rabbi Dosa.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיג רַבִּי דּוֹסָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa disagrees only
with the Rabbis
when it is at the time of her cycle,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת וִסְתָּהּ מוֹדֵי לְהוּ,
phrases.english: but when it is not at the time of her cycle, he agrees with them,
phrases.notes: He agrees that she is impure for the 24 hours before.

phrases.english: and our משנה is about the time of her cycle
and it follows Rabbi Dosa,
phrases.notes: So the משנה is not everyone's view after all, the opposite of what step 29 said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 30's question by moving the dispute to the usual-time case, which replaces step 29's approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the dispute the other way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about stains can only follow the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי דוסא agrees to מעת לעת at an unusual time, so the ברייתא fits him. The משנה, about her usual time, follows רבי דוסא alone.
